founder_preference: consumer-facing visual or transformation apps similar to photo-to-video; prosumer utilities are acceptable only as a fallback

method.warning: The 1-5 fields are transparent desk-research heuristics. They are not Apple monthly search volume, revenue, success probability, a v4 opportunity score, or a build decision.

dimensions.public_demand_proxy: 1-5 inference from relevant US App Store listings, rating accumulation, result density and chart presence; rating is E2/supporting only
dimensions.purchase_intent_proxy: 1-5 inference from visible one-time purchases, subscriptions, credits and task urgency; listed prices are not transactions
dimensions.competition: 1-5, where 5 is the hardest incumbent environment
dimensions.solo_readiness: 1-5 qualitative synthesis of bounded scope, technical feasibility and ongoing operational load, where 5 is strongest
dimensions.founder_style_fit: 1-5 fit with the founder's stated preference for visual, consumer and transformation-style mobile apps

method.priority_rule: fatal risk and evidence first, then the cheapest decisive test, solo operational burden, and founder preference; no composite ranking formula is used
method.review_sampling: Visible US App Store web reviews and Apple most-recent RSS pages form a non-random convenience sample. No theme prevalence or market percentage is inferred.

source_roots.note: Each entry maps a source to the primary artifact it comes from; sources sharing a root are one source, not independent corroboration. Granularity is document-level: two listings by the same seller get separate roots because seller identity was not collected in this pass. Do not compare these roots with analyses that use publisher-level roots.

research_actions.USER_BEHAVIOR_TEST: A working task prototype must beat the current workflow and request real refundable payment.
research_actions.TECHNICAL_RAT: A bounded corpus test must pass before demand or UI investment.
research_actions.TASK_AND_PAYMENT_TEST: A real triggered use case must complete and request real refundable payment.
research_actions.WEDGE_PAYMENT_TEST: The narrow workflow must be preferred over a strong free/incumbent substitute and receive real payment.
research_actions.COMPLIANCE_RAT: The scoped product must be checked against current official rules and real outcomes before wider product work.
research_actions.PARK_PREFERENCE_MISMATCH: Commercially credible but outside the founder's preferred product class; revisit only if that constraint changes.

direct_observations: The representative app shows about 2.1K US ratings and multiple subscription and lifetime price points.
A 2024 visible review says saving requires a subscription; 2025-2026 most-recent reviews report crashes, limited trial value and support/cancellation friction.
A new offline one-time competitor weakens privacy or one-time pricing as a standalone wedge.
candidates.wedge: Anchor-based alignment of 2-24 dated progress photos into a one-tap 9:16 proof video, rather than another two-photo compare editor.
candidates.price_hypothesis: $9.99-$14.99 lifetime after a usable free preview; no weekly subscription in MVP
candidates.killer_risk: The exact niche may be too small and users may stay with CapCut, Canva or manual crop even if alignment is faster.

first_test.assumption: Auto-align creates enough observable task advantage to cause real use and payment.
first_test.method: Twelve US iPhone users complete 20 real progress-photo sets in their current editor and in the prototype, then see a clearly disclosed $9.99 refundable preorder.
first_test.pass: At least 8/12 export within two minutes, 6/12 really share or use the result, and 4/12 place the preorder.
first_test.fail: Park if any threshold fails; narrow to one progress vertical if alignment is preferred but payment fails.

direct_observations: Multiple direct competitors show roughly 1.3K-17K ratings and paid unlocks or subscriptions.
Recent non-random reviews report missing picker assets, failure on a 6 GB video, a long job failing at 99 percent, and an output larger than the input.
Apple media APIs make on-device export possible, but average bitrate is not a guaranteed exact file-size contract across codecs and HDR formats.
candidates.wedge: Compress a user-selected video to a real 25 MB or 50 MB limit while preserving orientation, audio and capture date, with no ads and no full-library permission.

features: User-defined MB target and quality estimate

candidates.price_hypothesis: Two successful exports free, then $9.99-$12.99 lifetime; no weekly subscription in MVP
candidates.killer_risk: Exact-MB reliability can fail on real H.264, HEVC, HDR, edited, iCloud and multi-gigabyte assets, destroying the entire promise.

first_test.assumption: The encoder can reliably stay under a user target without producing worse failure modes than incumbents.
first_test.method: Run 30 stratified real videos across codec, HDR, resolution, frame rate, Photos-edited state, iCloud state and 2-6 GB size.
first_test.pass: At least 27/30 are no more than 2 percent over target; none becomes larger than source; audio and orientation survive; no crash or 99-percent stall; P90 export time is no more than 2x video duration on the test device.
first_test.fail: Drop the exact claim or park the product before building the full UI.

direct_observations: A dedicated birthday app shows about 1.6K ratings and a paid subscription ladder; broad slideshow incumbents show about 17K and 104K ratings.
A recent review praises ease, while other visible reviews report an exported greeting not opening for the recipient and ads blocking the flow.
Broad slideshow reviews also surface project loss, restart and payment-without-output problems, but the sample is not stratified.
candidates.wedge: Twelve photos, a name and one voice note become a finished birthday reel in under five minutes, with autosave and no licensed-music catalog dependency.

features: Automatic crop, duration and motion for 8-30 photos
Crash-safe autosave with local 9:16 and 16:9 export

candidates.price_hypothesis: $4.99 event export or $14.99 lifetime; no weekly subscription in MVP
candidates.killer_risk: The occasion keyword may be too small while free Photos, iMovie, Canva and CapCut remain good-enough substitutes.

first_test.assumption: A triggered birthday user values the bounded workflow enough to finish, share and pay.
first_test.method: Twelve US iPhone users with a real occasion in the next 30 days use their own 8-30 photos and see a disclosed $9.99 refundable preorder.
first_test.pass: At least 8/12 export within five minutes, 6/12 actually share or show it at the occasion, and 4/12 place the preorder.
first_test.fail: Park the standalone app if any threshold fails; retain memorial or birthday wording only as a query test or template inside a broader product.

direct_observations: Photomyne shows about 93K ratings, Google PhotoScan about 89K, and Photo Scanner Plus about 22K; Google is a strong free substitute.
Visible reviews describe thousands of scans, but also cropped edge notes, difficult computer or cloud export, weak naming and album organization, and fear of archive lock-in.
Photomyne already offers multi-photo capture, back-side scans, metadata and AI extras, so a feature checklist is not a credible wedge.
candidates.wedge: A local-first archival delivery workflow: preserve original plus crop, pair front and back, create deterministic filenames, and export JPG plus CSV or JSON manifest in one ZIP.

features: Front-back pairing with manual date and note

candidates.price_hypothesis: First 20 scans free, then $19.99 one-time Full Archive Export; test $14.99 and $24.99 alternatives
candidates.killer_risk: The archival export wedge may not overcome free Google or full-featured Photomyne, while any data-loss bug causes disproportionate trust and support damage.

first_test.assumption: People with a real archive project pay for portability and trust rather than more AI features.
first_test.method: Twelve US users with at least 100 physical photos scan 50 with their current tool and 50 with a concierge prototype, then face a real $19.99 archive-export payment.
first_test.pass: At least 6/12 pay, 8/12 prefer the archive delivery, critical crop or pairing loss stays below 2 percent, and the workflow is no more than 20 percent slower than the chosen incumbent.
first_test.fail: Do not build another generic scanner; park or narrow to a single archival handoff job.

direct_observations: The representative specialist shows about 7.5K ratings; adjacent specialists expose subscriptions, lifetime offers and even per-photo or credit pricing.
Recent non-random reviews report wrong colors, faces being changed, extra people or body parts, and restore actions that add unwanted facial features.
Positive visible reviews explicitly describe bringing family photos to life and sharing the results on Facebook.
candidates.wedge: A geometry-preserving colorizer that never invents a new face, keeps the original, and lets the user locally correct hair, skin and clothing colors.
candidates.price_hypothesis: Three photos free, then $14.99 lifetime if inference is on-device; otherwise test a transparent $2.99 ten-photo pack
candidates.killer_risk: Wrong colors and identity changes damage an emotional artifact, while an API model can change quality or cost without notice.

first_test.assumption: A bounded color-only workflow can produce trustworthy results across difficult family photos with controllable delivered cost.
first_test.method: Run an on-device candidate model on 50 permissioned historical photos across age, skin tone, damage and group size, then let ten real photo owners evaluate results without seeing which configuration produced them.
first_test.pass: At least 85 percent show no identity or geometry change and at least 8/10 owners keep one output; old-device latency and model size must also fit the release scope.
first_test.fail: Park the generic colorizer or narrow to a better-supported photo class.

representative_app.name: Passport Photo - ID Photo
representative_app.visible_price_signal: $5.99 remove ads; $9.99 one-time color or background unlock

direct_observations: Direct competitors show roughly 1.5K-21K ratings and one-time purchases, while some market biometric or baby calibration claims.
Visible reviews include an infant crop or head-size rejection, poor hair separation, surprise export paywalls and repeated crop attempts.
The US Department of State requires an original unchanged photo and explicitly rejects app, filter or AI edits, including digital background replacement.
candidates.wedge: A US-only baby capture coach that improves the physical setup and ranks burst frames without changing face or background pixels or claiming acceptance.

features: Physical setup, lighting and pose guidance
On-device blur, face visibility and pose ranking

candidates.price_hypothesis: $6.99 one-time US Baby Passport Export after a free setup and preview
candidates.killer_risk: A false 'good' signal can lead to a rejected or delayed application and a refund or trust burden that a solo developer must absorb.

first_test.assumption: An unedited capture coach can produce a usable frame quickly enough that real parents pay and submit it.
first_test.method: Fifteen US parents with a real child passport application in the next 60 days use a TestFlight or concierge prototype, pay a disclosed refundable $6.99, and report any photo-related resubmission request.
first_test.pass: At least 10/15 pay, median capture time is under five minutes, and at least 90 percent receive no photo-related resubmission request; never market the small sample as an acceptance guarantee.
first_test.fail: Remove compliance language or park the app; never add AI background replacement to rescue the result.

direct_observations: Motionleap shows about 117K ratings; modern AI video competitors show tens of thousands of ratings, category visibility, weekly prices and coin systems.
Recent AI Video reviews report outputs that do not follow the chosen motion, misleading unlimited claims, extra per-generation payment and slow or low-quality results.
Runway lists $0.01 per credit; a five-second Gen-4 Turbo generation is about $0.25 and Gen-4.5 about $0.60 before retries, storage, payment fees and support.
candidates.wedge: Three respectful, speech-free motions for old family portraits, with identity-quality rejection, automatic failed-job credit refund and explicit deletion.

features: Provider job plus identity and failure gate with automatic refund

candidates.price_hypothesis: Five clips for $9.99 with automatic technical-failure credit return; no unlimited subscription in MVP
candidates.killer_risk: Identity distortion, retries, provider changes, moderation, photo lifecycle, refunds and support turn a small UI into a high-operations AI service.

first_test.assumption: Respectful old-photo motion can meet identity and cost thresholds before any customer acquisition work.
first_test.method: Run 40 permissioned portraits and group photos through two providers using the same three motions and a predeclared acceptance rubric.
first_test.pass: At least 80 percent are acceptable on the first attempt or one retry, zero severe wrong-person or identity swaps occur, and average delivered inference cost is at most $1.20.
first_test.fail: Switch provider or motion scope once; otherwise park before building payments, queue or full app UI.

direct_observations: Two direct incumbents show about 32K and 19K ratings with paid batch, unlock and subscription products.
Recent non-random reviews report blurred exports, batch color limitations, app launch failures after purchase, five-photo limits and an unwanted app logo.
The core can run locally without backend, AI or moderation, making ongoing operations unusually light.
candidates.wedge: Stable 1-100-photo watermark batches for Etsy, eBay and Marketplace sellers, preserving pixel size and color profile with reusable relative-position presets.

features: Full-resolution batch export with per-item retry

candidates.price_hypothesis: Three photos and one preset free, then $7.99 lifetime; subscription only after real ongoing cloud or team value exists
candidates.killer_risk: The market is crowded and the best segment is a seller workflow, which conflicts with the founder's preferred consumer visual-product direction.

first_test.assumption: Active sellers pay for stable large-batch quality rather than using an incumbent or desktop tool.
first_test.method: Fifteen active sellers or photographers process a real 20-50-photo batch and see a $5 refundable deposit or $7.99 preorder.
first_test.pass: At least 10/15 finish without help in three minutes and at least 4 place the deposit.
first_test.fail: Park; do not broaden into a generic photo editor.

controls.reason: Dedicated exact-query traction remains weak; merge it into Occasion Reel until Apple Ads Search Popularity and paid conversion prove a standalone app.
Existing Quick Scan has evidence D and CORE_FEASIBILITY_BLOCKED unknown. iOS cannot justify a universal detector promise; only an honest guided room-check corpus is testable.
